title: Comparative analysis and innovation of a simple and rapid method for high-quality RNA and DNA extraction of kiwifruit
author: Afshar-Mohammadian, Rezadoost, et al.
materials: Extraction method using an RNeasy Plant Mini Kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Prepare fruit tissue
steps.instruction: Weigh 200 mg of kiwifruit outer pericarp (green part without seeds) and place it in a 2‑ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Add extraction buffer and homogenize
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml extraction buffer 1, 4 % (w/v) polyvinylpolypyrrolidone (PVPP) and 2 % (v/v) β‑mercaptoethanol to the tube, grind the tissue with a TissuRuptor, vortex for 20 s, then incubate in a heat sink at 65 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: First sodium acetate addition
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice for 5 min, then add 1/4 volume of 2 M sodium acetate (≈250 µl).

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction (first)
steps.instruction: Keep the tube on ice for another 5 min, add 500 µl phenol : chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (25 : 24 : 1, v/v), vortex for 1 min, and centrifuge at 12 000 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and repeat acetate
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µl of the upper aqueous phase to a new tube, add 1/4 volume of 2 M sodium acetate (≈175 µl), and place the tube on ice for 5 min.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction (second)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl phenol : chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (25 : 24 : 1, v/v), vortex for 1 min, and centrifuge at 14 000 rpm for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: LiCl precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µl of the supernatant to a new tube, add LiCl to a final volume equal to 1/2 of the total volume (i.e., add 350 µl of 2 M LiCl), and keep on ice for 20 min.

steps.title: Isopropanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 900 µl isopropanol, store the mixture at –20 °C for 1 h, then centrifuge at 14 000 rpm at 4 °C for 20 min to pellet the RNA.

steps.title: Ethanol wash (first)
steps.instruction: Gently add 70 % ethanol to the pellet, let stand for 2 min at room temperature without mixing, then centrifuge at 8 000 rpm for 2 min. Avoid spilling the pellet.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform re‑extraction
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 300 µl DEPC‑treated water, add 500 µl phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (25 : 24 : 1, v/v), vortex briefly, and centrifuge at 13 000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Second isopropanol precipitation
steps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous supernatant to a new tube, add 1 ml isopropanol, place on ice for 5 min, then centrifuge at 14 000 rpm at 4 °C for 20 min to recover the RNA pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol wash (second)
steps.instruction: Add 70 % ethanol gently, let stand 2 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at 8 000 rpm for 2 min. Avoid disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Final resuspension and storage
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet briefly, dissolve it in 50 µl DEPC‑treated water, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare DNA tissue
steps.instruction: Weigh 200 mg of kiwifruit outer pericarp and place it in a 2‑ml microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Add DNA extraction buffer and homogenize
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml extraction buffer 1, 4 % (w/v) PVPP and 2 % (v/v) β‑mercaptoethanol, grind with a TissuRuptor, vortex for 20 s, then incubate at 65 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: First phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice for 10 min, add 500 µl phenol : chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (25 : 24 : 1, v/v), vortex 1 min, and centrifuge at 12 000 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Second phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µl of the aqueous phase to a new tube, add 500 µl phenol : chloroform : isoamyl alcohol (25 : 24 : 1, v/v), vortex 1 min, and centrifuge at 10 000 rpm for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Sodium acetate addition
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µl of the supernatant to a fresh tube and add 1/2 volume of 2 M sodium acetate (≈350 µl).

steps.title: Isopropanol precipitation (DNA)
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice for 15 min, add 800 µl isopropanol, keep on ice for 30 min, then centrifuge at 12 000 rpm for 20 min at 4 °C to pellet DNA.

steps.title: Ethanol wash (DNA)
steps.instruction: Add 70 % ethanol gently, let stand 2 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at 8 000 rpm for 2 min. Avoid spilling the pellet.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform re‑extraction (DNA)
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 300 µl nuclease‑free water, add 500 µl phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (25 : 24 : 1, v/v), vortex briefly, and centrifuge at 13 000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final isopropanol precipitation (DNA)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl isopropanol, place on ice for 5 min, then centrifuge at 14 000 rpm at 4 °C for 10 min to collect the DNA pellet.

steps.title: Ethanol wash (final DNA)
steps.instruction: Add 70 % ethanol gently, let stand 2 min at room temperature, then centrifuge at 8 000 rpm for 2 min.

steps.title: Final DNA resuspension
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the DNA pellet, dissolve in 50 µl nuclease‑free water, and store at –80 °C.

description: Some protocols such as those described by Smart and Roden [1], Minguzzi et al. [4], Ma et al. [5], and Yockteng et al. [6] which are used for RNA extraction from plant tissues had low yield because of the high amount of polyphenols, polysaccharides and other secondary metabolites in the plant tissues. Meanwhile, most of the examined isolation methods were complicated. By the way, the extraction techniques and the quality of the products, the relative analysis of genomes or transcriptomes across plant and tissue types bring a challenge for researchers. The majority of the protocols are not completely satisfying as they may be time using up, technically complicated, need ultracentrifugation steps and are specific to a particular plant species. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a highly efficient method for RNA and DNA extraction from kiwifruit. Purity and concentration of RNA and DNA, extracted by different examined methods came in Table 1, Table 2. The results showed that the average yields of total RNA from fruit and leaf of A. deliciosa was ∼2180.7 ng/μl (∼545.175 μg/g FW) and ∼3424.9 ng/μl (∼856.225 μg/g FW), respectively. Absorption of A260/A230 and A260/A280 ratios in our new protocol (Regular Procedure) was higher than 2.0 using indicating the high purity of RNA samples without polyphenols and polysaccharides contamination. Also, the high absorption of A260/A280 ratios indicates a very low proteins contamination. On the other hand, the average absorption of A260/A230 of RNA examined using other protocols ranged from 0.15 to 2.02 and the average absorption of A260/A280 from 1.33 to 2.0 indicating the samples contamination by polyphenols, polysaccharides and proteins. Nevertheless, the average RNA yields using other protocols were far less and ranged from 28.09 to 14,445.6 ng/μl.
